statements.claim: Krishna came before the elders, Nanda at their head, bowed low, and asked what ceremony they had undertaken.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.1-2: Krishna, bowing humbly, asked the elders led by Nanda: 'kathyatāṃ me pitaḥ ko 'yaṃ sambhramo...' (verse 2).

statements.claim: He asked four things: what the ceremony is, its fruit, for whom it is meant, and by what means it is accomplished.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.2: 'kiṃ phalaṃ kasya voddeśaḥ kena vā sādhyate makhaḥ'.

statements.claim: His eagerness to hear was real and large; he asked as one who truly wished the answer.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.3: 'etad brūhi mahān kāmo mahyaṃ śuśrūṣave pitaḥ'.

statements.claim: The text marks that he was the Lord who knows all things, the Self of every being, the one who sees everything.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.1: 'tad-abhijño 'pi bhagavān sarvātmā sarva-darśanaḥ'.

statements.claim: People perform their rites whether they understand them or not, and acting with understanding is not the same as acting without it.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.5: 'jñatvājñātvā ca karmāṇi jano 'yam anutiṣṭhati'; viduṣaḥ karma-siddhiḥ syād yathā nāviduṣo bhavet.

statements.claim: Before anything else he wanted to know what the elders had settled upon, and why.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.6: 'tatra tāvat kriyā-yogo bhavatāṃ kiṃ vicāritaḥ'.

statements.claim: The sacrifice had come down from the elders' fathers and their fathers before them, season after season.
statements.evidence: Inherited tradition is the story's framing; the 'paramparyāgata' dharma is stated in Nanda's speech (10.24.10).

statements.claim: The question hung in the air over Vraja, simple and unsettling.
statements.evidence: Atmosphere; no sourceable fact asserted.

notes: Every factual claim tracks BP 10.24.1-6 closely; no unsupported or contradicted material.

statements.claim: Indra is lord of the clouds and rain, king of the celestials; the clouds are his own forms.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.7 (in pack passage): 'parjanyo bhagavān indro meghās tasyātma-mūrtayaḥ'.

statements.claim: This season the cowherds, at a boy's word, carried their offerings to a hill instead of Indra.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.30-37 in pack; 10.25.1: 'indras tadātmanaḥ pūjāṃ vijñāya vihatāṃ'.

statements.claim: The boy had argued beings are born and perish by their own deeds, clouds rain by nature, and forest people should honour what they live by.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.13-23 (karmaṇaiva, rajasā coditā meghā, vanaukasas... vana-śaila-nivāsinaḥ).

statements.claim: The cowherds walked in a circle around the hill, cows and brahmins, the women of Vraja singing of the boy's deeds.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.32-33: 'giriṃ cakruḥ pradakṣiṇam'; 'gopyaś ca kṛṣṇa-vīryāṇi gāyantyaḥ'.

statements.claim: The boy came before the hill, said 'I am the mountain,' and in a great form received the offerings.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.34: 'śailo 'smīti bruvan bhūri balim ādad bṛhad-vapuḥ'.

statements.claim: When Indra understood his worship had been cut off, he grew angry with the cowherds whose lord was Krishna, Nanda and the rest.
statements.evidence: BP 10.25.1: 'gopebhyaḥ kṛṣṇa-nāthebhyo nandādibhyaś cukopa ha'.

statements.claim: Indra had come to expect the cowherds' homage season after season, an old arrangement.
statements.evidence: Consistent with the inherited Indra-yajna tradition (10.24.8-10, Harivamsha 1.70).

statements.claim: The anger gathered over Vraja like a storm not yet broken.
statements.evidence: Atmospheric framing of the following beat.

notes: Faithful expansion of BP 10.25.1 plus recapitulation fully grounded in 10.24 passages included in the pack.

statements.claim: Nanda told Krishna that Indra is the lord of the clouds, and the clouds are his very selves, raining down the delight and life of all beings.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.7: 'parjanyo bhagavān indro meghās tasyātma-mūrtayaḥ / te 'bhivarṣanti bhūtānāṃ prīṇanaṃ jīvanaṃ payaḥ'.

statements.claim: He and all other men worship Indra with offerings produced by his own rain.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.8: 'vārmucāṃ patim īśvaram / dravyais tad-retasā siddhair yajante kratubhir narāḥ'.

statements.claim: On what remains after the offering the people live, pursuing the good things a life is meant to hold.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.9: 'tac-cheṣeṇopajīvanti tri-varga-phala-hetave' (tri-varga = the three aims of life).

statements.claim: It is a dharma that has come down from the fathers and the fathers' fathers, handed down without a break.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.10: 'dharmaṃ paramparyāgataṃ'.

statements.claim: A man may abandon it out of desire, hatred, fear or greed, but the one who sets it aside does not come to anything good.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.10: 'kāmād dveṣād bhayāl lobhāt sa vai nāpnoti śobhanam'.

statements.claim: Without the rain the grass would not grow, the cows would not graze, the milk would not come.
statements.evidence: Natural elaboration of verse 7's claim that rain is the life of beings; no specific verse asserts the milk detail.

statements.claim: Nanda gave the answer simply, without pride, and waited to see what the boy would make of it.
statements.evidence: Narrative characterization; consistent with the speech's tone.

notes: Direct, faithful rendering of BP 10.24.7-10; all doctrinal content sourced.

statements.claim: A being is born by its own actions and comes to its end by them; joy, sorrow, fear and safety are all reached through one's deeds.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.13: 'karmaṇā jāyate jantuḥ karmaṇaiva pralīyate / sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ bhayaṃ kṣemaṃ karmaṇaivābhipadyate'.

statements.claim: A lord who hands out the fruits of others' deeds only follows the actor; he has no power over one who has done nothing.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.13: 'asti ced īśvaraḥ... kartāraṃ bhajate so 'pi na hy akartuḥ prabhur hi saḥ'.

statements.claim: Among tilling, trading, tending cattle and lending, the cowherds' livelihood has always been cattle.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.20: 'kṛṣi-vāṇijya-go-rakṣā kusīdaṃ... vayaṃ go-vṛttayo 'niśam'.

statements.claim: The clouds rain not by a king's command but driven by rajas, nature's restless force, in every direction.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.21-22: 'sattvaṃ rajas tama iti... rajasā coditā meghā varṣanty ambūni sarvataḥ'.

statements.claim: Whoever thrives by one thing and bows to another finds no security; whoever is helped by one and worships another meets calamity in this world and the next.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.18 ('na tasmād vindate kṣemaṃ'); Harivamsha 1.71: 'visited by twofold calamities in this world, and in the next after death'.

statements.claim: He compared such a man to a faithless woman who leaves her own home for strangers and keeps nothing.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.18: 'jārān nāry asatī yathā'.

statements.claim: We have no cities, no towns, no walled houses; we are people of the forest who live among forests and hills.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.23: 'na naḥ purojanapadā na grāmā na gṛhā vayam / vanaukasas... vana-śaila-nivāsinaḥ'.

statements.claim: Let the sacrifice be for the cows, the brahmins and the hill.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.24: 'tasmād gavāṃ brāhmaṇānām adreś cārabhyatāṃ makhaḥ'.

statements.claim: He prescribed the details: take the offerings gathered for Indra, cook the rich dishes and milk-rice, brahmins feed the fires, food to every guest even the lowliest, fodder to the cows, oblation to the hill, then circumambulate the cows, brahmins, fire and mountain.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.25-28: pāyasa/saṃyāva, 'hūyantām agnayaḥ... brāhmaṇair', 'annaṃ bahu-guṇaṃ tebhyo deyaṃ', 'anyebhyaś cāśva-cāṇḍāla-patitebhyo yathārhataḥ', 'yavasaṃ ca gavāṃ dattvā giraye dīyatāṃ baliḥ', 'pradakṣiṇāṃ ca kuruta go-viprānala-parvatān'.

statements.claim: 'This is my thought, father... Do it, if it pleases you. This sacrifice to the cows, the brahmins and the hills is dear to me.'
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.29: 'etan mama mataṃ tāta kriyatāṃ yadi rocate / ayaṃ go-brāhmaṇādrīṇāṃ mahyaṃ ca dayito makhaḥ'.

statements.claim: He was the Lord of time itself who had set out to break Indra's pride.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.31: 'kālātmanā bhagavatā śakra-darpa-jighāṃsayā'.

statements.claim: The cowherds agreed to do exactly as he said.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.31: 'sādhv agṛhṇanta tad-vacaḥ'.

notes: Dense but every claim maps to 10.24.13-29 or the parallel Harivamsha/VP excerpts; zero drift.

statements.claim: Every year the people of Vraja set aside a day for Indra; this year, at a boy's urging, they set it aside instead and prepared to honour Govardhana.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.30-32; index summary 'Nanda and the cowherds accept Krishna's words and perform the sacrifice to Govardhana hill'.

statements.claim: They brought offerings to the hill, to the cows and to the brahmins.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.31-32: 'upahṛtya balīn samyag... yavasaṃ gavām'.

statements.claim: The villagers climbed onto their decorated bullock carts and, with their cattle before them, walked around Govardhana keeping the hill on their right.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.32-33: 'go-dhanāni puraskṛtya giriṃ cakruḥ pradakṣiṇam'; 'anāṃsy anaḍud-yuktāni te cāruhya sv-alaṅkṛtāḥ'.

statements.claim: Krishna took on another form, vast and still, stood upon the summit of the hill and said 'I am the hill.'
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.34: 'kṛṣṇas tv anyatamaṃ rūpaṃ... śailo 'smīti bruvan... bṛhad-vapuḥ'; VP 5.10: 'Upon the summit of Govarddhana, Krishńa presented himself, saying "I am the mountain"'.

statements.claim: That form began to eat, consuming the abundant offerings.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.34: 'bhūri balim ādad'; VP 5.10: 'partook of much food presented by the Gopas'.

statements.claim: The people of Vraja bowed low and murmured 'Behold, the hill has favored us.'
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.35-36: 'tasmai namo vraja-janaiḥ saha cakra'; 'aho paśyata śailo 'sau rūpī no 'nugrahaṃ vyadhāt'.

statements.claim: Krishna had argued the hill's grass nourished the cows and its slopes held the clouds.
statements.evidence: Recap of the preceding argument (10.24.17-24); the cloud-holding detail is a nature description, not a pack claim.

statements.claim: The walking-around was an old gesture that bound them to the hill.
statements.evidence: Reflective framing of the circumambulation.

notes: Worship and manifestation beats both match BP 10.24.30-37; summit detail corroborated by VP 5.10.

statements.claim: Indra, furious, summoned the Samvartaka clouds, the storm-clouds of dissolution kept for the ending of an age.
statements.evidence: BP 10.25.1: 'gaṇaṃ sāṃvartakaṃ nāma meghānāṃ cānta-kārīṇām'; Harivamsha 1.73: 'the clouds called Samvartaka'.

statements.claim: He told them: if you respect your king, Nanda and these cowherds have grown hostile to my festival.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.73: 'if you cherish any respect for your king... Nanda and other Gopas have grown inimical towards my festival'.

statements.claim: Within seven nights they were to afflict with rain and wind the precious cattle, the animals from which the cowherds take their very name.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.73: 'within seven nights, distress, with rain and winds, the precious kine which constitute their life-long subsistence and for which they pass by the name of Gopas'.

statements.claim: Indra himself would ride his elephant Airavata and pour down rain and wind flashing like thunder and lightning.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.73: 'I myself, stationed on (my elephant) Airavata, shall discharge dreadful rain, winds and showers effulgent like thunder and lightning'.

statements.claim: The clouds would drive the cattle to destruction.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.73: 'you will kill all the kine and the inhabitants of Vraja'; BP 10.25.1-8 excerpt.

statements.claim: The clouds rolled up dark-blue and vast as mountains, muttering, some like elephants, some like sea-creatures, some like serpents, and made an unfair day.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.73: 'dreadful dark-blue clouds, resembling a mountain in size and muttering awfully... some resembling the elephants, some the Makaras and some the serpents... created a very unfair day'.

statements.claim: Lightning flared without pause; they wrapped the heavens in darkness, adorned with Indra's rainbow bow.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.73: 'Producing lightnings continually the clouds, adorned with the bow of Indra, enshrouded the welkin with darkness'.

statements.claim: The sun and moon vanished; the stars were swallowed.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.73: 'The planets and stars disappearing from view, the sky, shorn of the rays of the sun and the moon'.

statements.claim: Earth, horizon and sky were blended into one by the heavy shower, and people took it for a deep, unpassable ocean in the sky.
statements.evidence: VP 5.11: 'the earth, the points of the horizon, and the sky, were all blended into one by the heavy and incessant shower'; Harivamsha 1.73: 'a deep, unpassable and limitless ocean stationed in the sky'.

statements.claim: Rain fell in columns thick as pillars and streams wide as an elephant's trunk; rivers swelled and tore away bank trees.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.73: showers 'resembling... the trunks of elephants and some bamboos'; 'the rivers, increasing their size, carried away the trees grown on their banks'.

statements.claim: Grass and trees trembled as if rebuked by thunder; birds could not leave their nests; animals fled; peacocks cried out.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.73: grass and trees 'began to tremble'; 'the birds could not come out of their nests and the animals began to fly away'; 'The peacocks began to cry aloud'.

statements.claim: The cowherds, drenched and terrified, said the end of the world was at hand and the earth would become one sheet of water.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.73: 'We think the end of the world is at hand and the earth will be converted into one sheet of water'.

statements.claim: The cows stood motionless and lowed in distress, soaked, trembling, hair standing up; some died of exhaustion, some fled, some sank down in the cold with their calves.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.73: cows 'stood motionless and began to cry aloud... the hairs stood erect... Some died out of exhaustion, some took to their heels in fear and some with their calves sank under frost'.

statements.claim: The cows and calves looked toward Krishna and cried 'Save us! Save us!'
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.73: 'looked towards Krishna and cried "Save us! Save us!"'.

statements.claim: Krishna understood why the storm had come and had already begun to plan.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.73: Krishna 'greatly worked up with anger... meditating for a while... "To protect them... I will uproot this best of mountains Govardhana"'.

statements.claim: He was not a god who forgave such things; his fury rose.
statements.evidence: Characterization consistent with 10.25.1 (cukopa) and the Harivamsha mandate.

notes: Storm sequence tracks Harivamsha 1.73 nearly line-for-line; counts (seven nights) and cattle-death details match. 'Kept apart for the ending of an age' is a fair reading of cānta-kārīṇām/Samvartaka.

statements.claim: Krishna had uprooted Govardhana and lifted it over the cowherds like an umbrella; villagers and cattle crowded beneath it.
statements.evidence: Recap of the immediately preceding canonical beat (previous story 'Krishna Lifts Govardhana Hill'); BP 10.25.20 addresses the held hill ('mad-dhastādri-nipātanāt').

statements.claim: Hunger and thirst pressed on them; they set aside hunger, thirst, aches and longing for comfort.
statements.evidence: BP 10.25.22: 'kṣut-tṛḍ-vyathāṃ sukhāpekṣāṃ hitvā'.

statements.claim: Krishna told them there was nothing to fear; the hill would not fall on them while he held it.
statements.evidence: BP 10.25.20: 'na trāsa iha vaḥ kāryo mad-dhastādri-nipātanāt'.

statements.claim: Their minds steadied by his word, they went in and stayed.
statements.evidence: BP 10.25.21: 'nirviviśur gartaṃ kṛṣṇāśvāsita-mānasaḥ'.

statements.claim: Seven days Krishna stood holding the hill without moving from his place.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'he held the mountain for seven days without moving from his place' (BP 10.25, verses 19-23 rendering).

statements.claim: Indra, seeing the cowherds sheltered by a mountain held by a boy, was astonished; his anger gave way and he checked his clouds.
statements.evidence: BP 10.25.23: 'kṛṣṇa-yogānubhāvaṃ taṃ niśamyendro 'ti-vismitaḥ'; excerpt: 'Indra, astonished, checked his clouds'.

statements.claim: The rain slackened, the wind died, the clouds drew apart and the sun came out.
statements.evidence: BP 10.25.24: 'khaṃ vyabhram uditādityaṃ vāta-varṣaṃ ca dāruṇam' (sky cloudless, sun risen, fierce wind and rain gone).

statements.claim: The cowherds were told to come out, leaving fear behind, with their women, wealth and children.
statements.evidence: BP 10.25.25: 'niryāta tyajata trāsaṃ gopāḥ sa-strī-dhanārbhakāḥ'.

statements.claim: The cowherds he meant to destroy were sheltered and dry; the boy had not stirred.
statements.evidence: Consistent with 10.25.23 (astonishment at Krishna's power) and the sheltered state; 'dry' is an implied corollary of the shelter.

notes: All claims grounded in BP 10.25.20-25; the lifting recap matches the corpus chain's prior beat.

statements.claim: The cowherds came out from beneath the hill, each gathering up what was his — the goods and the cattle.
statements.evidence: BP 10.25.26: 'niryayur gopāḥ svaṃ svam ādāya go-dhanam'.

statements.claim: Krishna set the mountain back down in its own place, as it had stood before.
statements.evidence: BP 10.25.27: 'śailaṃ sva-sthāne pūrva-vat'.

statements.claim: Nanda, Yashoda, Rohini and Balarama came to him and embraced him.
statements.evidence: BP 10.25.28-29: 'yaśodā rohiṇī nando rāmaś ca balināṃ varaḥ'; 'samīyuḥ parirambhaṇādibhiḥ'.

statements.claim: The gopis welcomed him with curd and unbroken rice, showering blessings with glad hearts.
statements.evidence: BP 10.25.28: 'gopyaś ca sa-sneham apūjayan mudā dadhy-akṣatādbhir yuyujuḥ sad-āśiṣaḥ'.

statements.claim: In heaven the hosts of gods — siddhas, sadhyas, gandharvas and charanas — rained flowers down on him.
statements.evidence: BP 10.25.30: 'divi deva-gaṇāḥ siddhāḥ sādhyā gandharva-cāraṇāḥ'; pack excerpt: 'the gods rained flowers'.

statements.claim: Conches and drums sounded in the sky.
statements.evidence: BP 10.25.31: 'śaṅkha-dundubhayo nedur divi'.

statements.claim: Krishna, surrounded by the devoted cowherds, set out with Balarama for his own cow-pen.
statements.evidence: BP 10.25.32: 'anuraktaiḥ paśupaiḥ pariśrito... sva-goṣṭhaṃ sa-balo 'vrajad dhariḥ'.

statements.claim: The land that had sheltered them closed over the gap where they had hidden.
statements.evidence: Imagery consistent with restoring the hill to its place; not a separate sourceable fact.

notes: Restoration, embrace and heavenly rejoicing all map to BP 10.25.26-32; characters and actions exact.
